headline: Iraq's foreign minister says outside actors are using Iraqi territory for attacks
body:
What happened: Iraq's foreign minister, Fuad Hussein, told Al Jazeera that Baghdad holds evidence that outside parties have used Iraqi territory to launch strikes on neighbouring states. Baghdad is probing attacks aimed at Gulf countries and is pursuing talks with Saudi Arabia over the dispute. Saudi Arabia has blamed Iran-aligned groups in Iraq for attacks on its oil infrastructure, and Iraq confirmed in September that drones hitting a Saudi pipeline came from Iraqi soil.

Hussein also said Iraq is negotiating with Iran-aligned factions to place their weapons under state control, and that Washington has asked for most border crossings with Iran to close. He added that Iraq lost about $60bn when Strait of Hormuz oil shipments were halted, and that shipments have resumed under understandings with the US and Iran.

Reported by: Al Jazeera

headline: Trump expected to meet Xi in Shenzhen after Republican midterm losses
body:
What happened: After Republicans lost control of both chambers of the US Congress in midterm elections, US President Donald Trump is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in about two weeks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' meeting in Shenzhen. The article notes that China hosted Barack Obama at a G20 summit in Hangzhou a decade earlier, when he was similarly weakened politically. If the meeting goes ahead, it would be the two leaders' third in-person encounter this year. The piece frames the Apec gathering as a test of whether Trump can reach lasting agreements with Beijing.

Reported by: SCMP. Also covered by Xinhua, China Daily, People's Daily, CGTN.

headline: Ukraine says Russia fired North Korean missiles in overnight attack
body:
What happened: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said Russian forces used North Korean-made KN-23 ballistic missiles in a large overnight strike on 6-7 November that hit a key energy facility. Of 36 missiles launched on a ballistic trajectory, he said only four were intercepted. Forensic examinations are still under way at the impact sites. Substations in several oblasts, including Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk, were damaged, and 12 regions beyond Kyiv were attacked. Nine people were injured, one of them a child.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Euronews.

headline: Russian strikes leave Kyiv short of power and water ahead of peace talks
body:
What happened: Russia launched a large overnight attack on Kyiv and surrounding regions, using 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles against electricity substations and a bridge over the Dnipro River. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes aimed to plunge the capital and the country into darkness, leaving residents facing power, water and heat problems; five people were injured, including a 14-year-old girl. Negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the US are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday. Russia's defence ministry said the strikes targeted energy and transport sites.

Reported by: The Guardian. Also covered by Ukrainska Pravda.

headline: Overnight Russian strikes deal fresh damage to Ukraine's power grid
body:
What happened: Overnight drone and ballistic missile attacks hit Ukrainian energy facilities, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky, causing blackouts and disrupting water supplies. He said 12 regions were struck, with Kyiv the hardest hit, and nine people were reported injured, including a child. Substations serving the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants were among those damaged. Zelensky said Moscow was intensifying attacks ahead of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week. Kyiv's mayor said the water system had returned to normal, and the energy minister reported power cuts in five regions.

Reported by: BBC News

headline: US strikes hit Qeshm as Hormuz shipping attacks and mediation efforts continue
body:
What happened: The United States struck Iran's Qeshm island after vessels were targeted in the Strait of Hormuz, while mediators work to stop a wider clash. Two projectiles reportedly hit the island on Friday night, part of a series of strikes on Iranian air defences and launchers in recent weeks. Iran's army said it downed a US MQ-9 drone, and the Revolutionary Guard claimed an MQ-1 interception. UKMTO reported at least 11 ships attacked around the strait in the week to November 6, with shipping traffic about 65 percent below pre-conflict levels.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard said limits on its missile range no longer apply, and Iran's foreign minister said he had held talks with 12 foreign ministers, including those of Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Al-Monitor, The New Arab.

headline: Vance pushes his own policy profile after Republican midterm losses
body:
What happened: After Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, Vice President JD Vance shifted his campaign messaging toward issues central to his own political identity, such as economic nationalism, foreign policy restraint and public safety. Reporting by Reuters, based on speeches and sources, says the move was deliberate and avoided President Donald Trump's signature policies, which polls suggested were weighing down Republican candidates.

Vance later blamed the Iran war for the defeat, called for a swift end to the conflict, and urged a rethink of the US relationship with Israel. Trump defended the war and said he would have done nothing differently, while Vance's allies say he is not breaking with the president. Analysts say the episode raises his standing as a possible 2028 contender, though Republican losses in states he campaigned in may complicate his brand.

Reported by: Dawn. Also covered by The Guardian, Jerusalem Post.

headline: Ukraine names Russian officers and pilots over deadly Komyshuvakha shelter strike
body:
What happened: Ukraine's military intelligence says it has identified Russian personnel it believes were involved in a November 2 airstrike on an underground school in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, where civilians were collecting aid. Local authorities put the death toll at no fewer than 55, with more than 50 others still missing and rescue work continuing for days. HUR named a Russian officer it says planned the attack, along with six pilots of Su-34 fighter-bombers, and said a seventh crew was still being identified. President Zelensky called for stronger air defence support from partners.

Reported by: Kyiv Independent. Also covered by Ukrainska Pravda.

headline: Deadly market strike in Taiz as Yemen's offensive against the Houthis intensifies
body:
What happened: A missile strike on a market in Taiz governorate in Yemen killed dozens on Friday, with each side blaming the other. The attack comes a month after Yemen's internationally recognised government, led by Rashad al-Alimi, launched its "Dawn of Yemen" offensive against the Iran-aligned Houthis, backed by Saudi-led coalition airstrikes. The government says it has recaptured several areas in Taiz and elsewhere, though it has also lost ground there. Hundreds of thousands have been displaced, and the government says its forces have carried out tens of thousands of operations, figures Al Jazeera could not verify.

Reported by: Al Jazeera

headline: Gaza's death toll climbs as hospitals report fresh deaths and injuries
body:
What happened: Medical sources in Gaza say hospitals recorded ten deaths and 22 injuries over the past two days, pushing the reported death toll to 74,640 and the wounded count to 175,947. Citing these sources, the Palestinian news agency Wafa says roughly 1,610 Palestinians have been killed and 5,819 wounded since a ceasefire took effect in October 2025, which it attributes to Israeli fire. Rescue teams have also recovered about 849 bodies from rubble, while thousands are thought to remain buried under destroyed buildings. These figures come from local health and agency sources and were not independently verified in the report.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Xinhua.

headline: Houthi media reports 11 dead in Saudi strikes near Sanaa
body:
What happened: Houthi-run media said Saturday that Saudi air strikes on homes in the Al-Shariyah area of Sanaa province killed 11 people, including women and children. The Saba news agency also said rescuers searching the rubble were still working to recover bodies, and claimed two strikes hit paramedics. The figures come from the Houthi side and could not be independently verified. The reported deaths come amid a renewed escalation in Yemen's long-running civil war.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Xinhua.

Government forces and local authorities rejected that account and accused the Houthis of indiscriminate fire instead. The report notes intense clashes in the province in recent weeks and says it hosts about half of the more than 300,000 people displaced by the latest fighting. The death toll and responsibility could not be independently confirmed from the material available.

headline: Tanker fire in Strait of Hormuz reportedly caused by naval mine
body:
What happened: Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. Separate statements from Iran's Revolutionary Guards and army, relayed by local media on Thursday, reported five oil tankers and a tugboat on fire in the waterway. The strait has been under heavy Iranian traffic restrictions since the Iran war began in late February. The claims could not be independently verified from the reporting available.

Reported by: Fars. Also covered by SCMP, The New Arab, Middle East Eye, Mehr News.

headline: Ukrainian missiles hit Russian plant in Oryol, fire reported
body:
What happened: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck the Proton-Elektroteks plant in the Russian city of Oryol during the night of 6-7 November, using Neptune missiles fired by the Ukrainian Navy. The army says the target was hit and a fire and explosions were seen at the facility. The extent of the damage had not yet been assessed. The factory makes optoelectronic equipment that Ukraine says feeds Russian missile programmes, including components for Kovyor cruise missiles and parts for Iskander-M ballistic missiles.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Kyiv Independent.

headline: Russia claims strikes on Kyiv bridge and plant as Ukraine's capital loses power
body:
What happened: Russia's Defence Ministry says it struck the Northern Bridge and the Meridian Plant near Kyiv overnight, describing the bridge as a military supply route and the plant as a cruise missile producer. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed the bridge strike and said the city faced severe problems with power, heating and water as temperatures fell to 0 degrees Celsius. Ukrainian officials reported one person killed and eight wounded. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles were used and called for more US support. The attack comes days before another round of US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by France 24.

headline: Ukraine's General Staff says Russian losses reached over 1.6 million troops
body:
What happened: Ukraine's General Staff reported on Nov. 7 that Russia has lost about 1,604,110 personnel since the full-scale invasion began on Feb. 24, 2022, including 2,280 over the previous day. The figures also list large numbers of lost tanks, armored vehicles, artillery systems and aircraft. Ukraine does not publish its own losses. Western think-tank estimates cited in the piece suggest Russian casualties substantially exceed Ukrainian ones, and Zelensky has said at least 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed.

Reported by: Kyiv Independent. Also covered by Ukrainska Pravda.

headline: Saudi coalition says it downed Houthi missile aimed at Medina region
body:
What happened: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said its air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile that the Houthis fired toward Medina. Saudi civil defence had issued a warning about possible danger near the port of Yanbu shortly before, and later said the threat had passed. The Houthis denied targeting the city, saying their attacks hit only oil facilities and military bases. Yanbu, a key oil export hub linked to the East-West pipeline, has been targeted by the Houthis several times recently. Separately, Yemeni government forces claimed gains in Taiz, which Al Jazeera could not independently verify.

headline: Russian overnight strike on Kyiv injures six, including a teenager
body:
What happened: Russian forces attacked Kyiv overnight on 6-7 November, causing fires in the Solomianskyi district and damage to homes, a kindergarten grounds building and a non-residential structure. Kyiv city officials and the State Emergency Service reported that six people were hurt, one of them a 14-year-old, after initially giving lower counts. A facade of a five-storey apartment block was partly destroyed, though no fire or deaths were reported there. Separately, a Russian drone reportedly hit a two-storey house in the Darnytskyi district, and firefighters contained several smaller blazes elsewhere in the city.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Kyiv Independent.

headline: Iran says its forces are stronger and on higher alert after war
body:
What happened: An Iranian army spokesman, Mohammad Akraminia, says the country's armed forces are stronger and more motivated than when the war with the United States and Israel began in February. He said the military has gained experience from direct confrontation and now has greater commitment and self-confidence. Akraminia also claimed Iran still controls the Strait of Hormuz and will keep it closed until Washington accepts Tehran's demands. He added that any military response, under the Supreme Leader's orders, would be immediate and not limited geographically. The statements were carried by the state news agency Irna and were not independently verified.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Asharq Al-Awsat, Al-Monitor, The New Arab, Dawn.

headline: North Korea's state-trained hackers linked to massive Binance crypto theft
body:
What happened: A Rappler report says North Korea has built a large, state-backed hacking force that recruits talented children early and rewards successful operatives with housing, cash shares of heist proceeds and party membership. The piece cites defectors and analysts, including a former trainer who fled to South Korea in 2004, and describes a program that selects about 150 to 200 students a year. It also says the group was behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack. The FBI and Binance have blamed North Korea, while Pyongyang denies involvement. South Korean intelligence estimated about 8,400 people work in the North's cyber operations.

Reported by: Rappler. Also covered by Reuters, Asharq Al-Awsat, Jerusalem Post.

headline: Traders shun Russian diesel shipments to US despite Trump-Putin arrangement
body:
What happened: Several tankers carrying Russian diesel that were bound for the United States have changed course, raising doubts about a deal Donald Trump announced with Vladimir Putin in October. Despite the arrangement, no diesel has yet reached the US, where retail prices have nearly doubled since the war on Iran began. Analysts say the volumes promised are small and would do little to ease supply, and the Treasury's temporary sanctions exemption remains contested. Terms of the deal, including price and payment, have not been made public by Washington or Moscow.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by AP, Al Jazeera, DW, France 24.

headline: Trump confirms US strikes on Iranian air defences near Qeshm Island
body:
What happened: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged American strikes on Iranian air defence systems on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, describing them as minor and brief. Iranian state media reported missile strikes in the Suza area and said Iranian forces shot down an American MQ-9 drone over the island. US Central Command described the situation as relatively calm and declined further comment. Trump also said Washington is in talks with Tehran and has made significant progress, without giving details. Qatar, which is mediating, rejected reports that negotiations had collapsed.

Reported by: AP. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, The Guardian, DW.

headline: US sanctions eight Canadian money firms accused of aiding Iran
body:
What happened: The US Treasury has imposed sanctions on eight money services businesses based in Ontario and British Columbia, alleging they handled transactions for sanctioned Iranian entities. The measures cut the firms off from the dollar-based financial system, freezing any US-held assets and barring dealings with American people and companies. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Canada should not serve as a refuge for those helping Iran's government evade sanctions. Separately, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network barred the offshore crypto exchange MEXC Global from US banking channels, citing alleged links to Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al Jazeera, The New Arab, Al-Monitor, Asharq Al-Awsat.

headline: Greek-owned tanker attack kills sailor as Iran reports burning ships in Hormuz
body:
What happened: A seafarer aboard a Greek-owned tanker was killed in an apparent missile strike in the Gulf, the company Velos Tankers said. The Marshall Islands-flagged vessel Velos Sapphire, travelling empty to Bahrain, was hit on Thursday and caught fire. Iranian state media and the Revolutionary Guards said several tankers were burning after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and blamed the American military for their route. The British maritime agency UKMTO reported a separate blast on a tanker off Oman, with its crew unharmed. The claims could not be independently verified.

Reported by: The New Arab. Also covered by Al-Monitor, Middle East Eye, Jerusalem Post, Daily Sabah.

headline: Ukraine says strikes have crippled much of Russia's oil refining capacity
body:
What happened: Ukrainian military intelligence says that by late September 2026, 15 of Russia's 38 main oil refineries were out of action and 12 more had cut output. Total refining at these plants fell 55.4% from the start of the year. The hardest-hit regions are the Volga, Central and Southern federal districts, where several major plants have stopped. Refineries in remote areas such as Omsk and Khabarovsk are still running and have partly offset shortages, though transport bottlenecks limit that. The intelligence service also claims the damage to Russia's oil sector exceeds $23.2 billion. These figures come from Ukraine's intelligence agency and could not be independently verified.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Kyiv Independent, Euronews, Meduza.

headline: Washington presses Beijing to deliver on rare earths and farm purchase pledges
body:
What happened: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer met Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng to press Beijing to carry out its commitments under the Busan trade agreement without delay. The US Treasury said continued progress depends on tangible results and that Washington will closely monitor implementation, also voicing concern over recent Chinese actions. China's commerce ministry responded that it is willing to buy more American farm products, but only if both sides put in place the agreed reciprocal tariff reduction of $30 billion each.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al Jazeera, DW, Japan Times, The Hindu.

headline: Syria reportedly sends military advisers to help Saudi Arabia against Houthis
body:
What happened: Two Syrian military sources and a senior US official say Damascus is providing Saudi Arabia with military advice and training as the kingdom faces Houthi attacks. Scores of personnel have reportedly travelled from Syria in recent weeks, and their mandate may be wider than advisory work. A Syrian diplomat called any deployment premature and said a Saudi-Syrian defence deal signed Wednesday covers advice, training and expertise exchange. A Saudi official said the cooperation mainly aims to restructure Syrian forces, and the Houthis and Saudi government did not respond to requests for comment.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al-Monitor, Middle East Eye, The New Arab, Jerusalem Post.

headline: Trump hints at sweeping Ukraine deal after meeting Putin's envoy
body:
What happened: U.S. President Donald Trump said he expects a major agreement on Ukraine that could extend to all of Europe, after meeting Kirill Dmitriev, the head of Russia's sanctioned sovereign wealth fund, at the White House on Thursday. Trump said he could not disclose what was discussed, though Russian and Ukrainian officials were also at an event that day where a temporary ceasefire around Oleshky was discussed. On Friday, Jared Kushner said Trump had raised the need for a broader European security framework with several European leaders. Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which began in February 2022, continues, and U.S.-brokered talks involving both sides are scheduled in Abu Dhabi for November 10-11.

Reported by: Politico Europe. Also covered by Reuters, BBC News, Al Jazeera, Le Monde.
